# Viz 1

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "A line graph shows simulated workout session durations from September 1 to October 25, 2026. Five colored lines represent push, pull, shoulders, legs, and cardio. Points mark individual sessions. Leg sessions last longest, while cardio duration varies most."

library(tidyverse)

# Load the detailed dataset
workout_details <- read_csv("workout_details.csv")

workout_details$date <- as.Date(workout_details$date)

# Put tennis in the Cardio category
workout_details$workout[
  workout_details$exercise == "Tennis"
] <- "Cardio"

# Keep one row per session
workouts <- workout_details %>%
  distinct(date, workout, session_duration_min)

# Create one graph with five lines
line_plot <- ggplot(
  workouts,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = session_duration_min,
    color = workout,
    group = workout
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = workout),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Push" = "#D55E00",
      "Pull" = "#0072B2",
      "Shoulders" = "#007A5E",
      "Legs" = "#444444",
      "Cardio" = "#882255"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 week",
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(40, 80),
    breaks = seq(40, 80, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "How long were my workout sessions?",
    subtitle = "Workout Log | September 1–October 25, 2026",
    x = "Session date",
    y = "Session duration (minutes)",
    color = "Workout type",
    shape = "Workout type",
    caption = paste(
      "Joseph Saputra | October 25, 2026",
      "Source: Workout App Tracker",
      "Points mark sessions; lines connect sessions of the same type.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 10)
  )

line_plot
```
